name: carrier_layers
title: What a transport-v2 tunnel byte is wrapped in
summary: From the inside out, the app's bytes are sealed, framed for their stream, and carried as a WebSocket message on an HTTP/2 stream inside TLS 1.3 over TCP. The network sees only the outer layers, and timing, sizes and volume stay observable.
comment: Layers are listed innermost first. The frame header sits outside the seal: the AEAD authenticates its type, stream and flags as associated data.
Transport v2 only. Check docs/protocol/YUME_2_0_WIRE.md before changing the order.

nodes.title: YOUR BYTES
nodes.note: Whatever the application sent. If the app already used HTTPS, this part is encrypted by the app itself as well.

nodes.title: SEALED
nodes.note: After authentication every message is sealed with its own AES-256-GCM key from the session ratchet, and that key is erased once used.

nodes.title: YUME FRAME
nodes.note: An 8-byte header gives the length, frame type, stream number and flags, so many app connections share one tunnel. The seal authenticates the type, stream and flags.

nodes.title: WEBSOCKET
nodes.note: Frames travel as WebSocket binary messages, opened with an RFC 8441 extended CONNECT the way a browser keeps a live channel open.

nodes.title: HTTP/2 STREAM
nodes.note: The WebSocket lives on one HTTP/2 stream, opened after the client has fetched the cover site's page and assets on the same connection.

nodes.title: TLS 1.3
nodes.note: Encrypts everything inside it. The handshake follows one captured browser profile. It hides content, not timing, sizes or volume.

nodes.title: TCP
nodes.note: What a network observer sees first: a TCP connection to the server's HTTPS port.
